SITUATION
A high-volume 300 mm logic fab making a mature logic device has seen functional die yield drop about 20% over the past six weeks, holding low across many lots. The dip began after a scheduled preventive-maintenance window on the etch and deposition tools. Process engineers' leading theories are a pressure or temperature setpoint drift, so they favor retuning those setpoints. Inline inspection has flagged more defects than usual on a mid-line layer. Standard tool logs read broadly within spec. The etch, deposition, clean, and filtration modules are all adjustable. You have a limited number of experiments; you may measure quantities and apply available process controls, alone or in combination. Determine what is really driving the loss and what to do about it.

OUTCOME OF INTEREST: WaferYield (higher_is_better)
BUDGET: 0/15 experiments used, 15 left (code is free).
TURNS: 0/32, 32 left. Interventions so far: 0.
data files for code: (none yet)
MEASURABLE SIGNALS (ids):
  m0: handler throughput
  m1: argon flow
  m2: chamber flow uniformity
  m3: scanner focus
  m4: chamber pressure
  m5: exposure dose
  m6: deposition rate
  m7: fab humidity
  m8: stage temperature
  m9: wafer yield
  m10: backside cooling
  m11: film uniformity index
  m12: rinse time

CONTROLS (ids):
  a0: set handler throughput range [0, 100]
  a1: set exposure dose range [0, 100]
  a2: set scanner focus range [0, 100]
  a3: set fab humidity range [0, 100]
  a4: filtration upgrade range [0, 100]
  a5: gettering anneal range [0, 100]
  a6: set rinse time range [0, 100]

RESULT OF LAST ACTION
(none yet)

YOUR MEMORY
(empty)
